_meta.title: Chinese star names with their modern identifications
_meta.scope: The 312 traditional asterisms of the three enclosures and the twenty-eight lunar lodges, together with the individual stars and deep-sky objects that names in the record corpus point to. The stars added by the Qing survey of 1752 are not collected, since no earlier text names them, nor are stars that carry no Chinese name. A name that denotes a group of stars carries the places of the stars its figure joins, so that a sighting recorded against the group can still be measured. The twelve stations (十二次) are kept as spans of the lodges, as the Jin treatise gives them; the field allocations attached to them, and character conversion tables, are outside this table.
_meta.fields: key = standard name in Simplified Chinese. hant = the same name in Traditional Chinese. kind = lodge, enclosure, officer, star, cluster or station. in = the asterism this entry belongs to. rom = romanisation. en/fr/es/it/ja = the sense of the name. alias = older, variant and alternative written forms. modern = the modern identification, either {hip, bf, proper, mag, con, ra, dec} for a star, where proper = the IAU proper name, en as the IAU writes it and fr/es/it/ja where the locale writes it otherwise, or {designation, ...} for other objects. members = the J2000 places, in degrees, of the stars the asterism's figure joins. src = whether the entry is machine-derived or established by hand. For a station, branch = its earthly branch, span = {from, to} as [lodge, degree within the lodge], and span_variants = the starting degree given by Fei Zhi and Cai Yong.
_meta.provenance: Asterism names, the European-language readings and the star identifications are drawn from the sky data of the companion project SubstellarAtlas, which in turn rests on Wikipedia, HYG and SIMBAD. Entries added by hand are marked as such. The Japanese column is derived by converting the Traditional Chinese name to present-day Japanese character forms, Japanese astronomy having kept the Chinese asterism names and only written them in its own forms. The Huihui star table of Yabuuchi Kiyoshi (1964) was consulted offline for comparison only, and none of its data is reproduced here. modern.ra/dec are J2000 equatorial coordinates in degrees without proper motion, since over five millennia the proper motion of a naked-eye star stays far below the precision at which a lodge boundary can be read from a text.
